subject: Qur'an & Tajweed
source: Adapted from the school Drive Quran folder (TPS Quran Tracker: tajweed rules by year, Years 1-6 progression); Qur'an text per the Madinah mushaf (Hafs 'an 'Asim)

lessons.title: Welcome back: noon sakinah and tanween
objectives: Recall sukoon, shaddah, madd and tanween from Year 1
Spot noon sakinah and tanween in words
Know that the letter after them changes how we say them

keywords.def: a noon carrying a sukoon: نْ
a double vowel at the end of a word, sounding like 'n'
giving every letter and rule its right, beautifully

starter: Bismillah. Recite Al-Fatihah from memory with a partner.
What does a sukoon tell us to do with a letter?
What are the three tanween sounds? (-an, -in, -un)

teach.heading: What is tajweed?
bullets: Tajweed means making the recitation beautiful and correct
We give each letter its right sound
We learn the rules so we do not make mistakes
teach.note: Start with adab: sit well, bismillah, listen. Explain that Allah told us in Surat Al-Muzzammil (73:4) to recite the Qur'an with tarteel, slowly and clearly. Ask: why do we practise slowly first?

teach.heading: Noon sakinah
bullets: A noon with a sukoon: نْ
It is read inside or between words
teach.note: Write أَنْعَمْتَ on the board and circle the noon. Children echo 'an-'amta'. Misconception: noon with a vowel (نَ) is NOT noon sakinah - only the sukoon one.

teach.heading: Tanween
bullets: Tanween is a double fathah, kasrah or dammah
It only comes at the end of a word
It sounds like a noon sakinah
teach.note: Show سَمِيعٌ and خُسْرٍ and a word ending -an. Say: tanween is a noon sakinah that is spoken but not written. Children say the sound for each of the three marks.

teach.heading: Four rules ahead
bullets: The letter AFTER noon sakinah or tanween decides the rule
This term: izhar, iqlab and ikhfa
teach.note: Preview as a story: the noon meets a new letter and behaves differently each time. Do not teach the rules yet - build curiosity. Keep the pace calm and recite together.

practice: Find the noon sakinah in أَنْعَمْتَ and read it.
Which of these has tanween: كِتَابٌ or كِتَابُ? Say the ending sound.
independent: Sort 8 words into 'noon sakinah' or 'tanween' (e.g. مِنْ، عَلِيمٌ، أَنْتَ، خُسْرٍ، يَنْهَىٰ، رَحِيمًا، مِنْهُ، كَثِيرًا)
Find a noon sakinah and a tanween in your mushaf page
Recite Al-Fatihah to a partner and tick each sukoon word
exit: Point to one noon sakinah and one tanween, then say each sound.
What does tajweed mean?
lessons.homework: Find three words with tanween in the Qur'an page you are learning and read them to a family member.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: colour noon sakinah red and tanween blue on a printed page. Stretch: find a noon sakinah in Al-Asr (hint: الْإِنسَانَ).

lessons.title: Izhar: saying the noon clearly
objectives: Name the six throat letters
Say noon sakinah and tanween clearly before them
Read examples from the Qur'an with izhar

keywords.def: ء ه ع ح غ خ: six letters from the throat

starter: Read: مِنْ and عَلِيمٌ. Which has noon sakinah and which has tanween?

teach.heading: Izhar means clear
bullets: We say the noon with no humming
We do not hide or blend it
teach.note: Say a clear 'n' with the tip of the tongue touching the gum above the front teeth. Contrast with a mumbled version so children hear the difference. Ask: what does izhar sound like?

teach.heading: The six throat letters
bullets: ء  ه  ع  ح  غ  خ
If one follows noon sakinah or tanween: izhar
teach.note: Teach the order with a rhythm: hamza, haa, 'ayn, Haa, ghayn, khaa. Point to the throat. Children touch their throat when saying each. Memory aid: a chant to a beat.

teach.heading: Examples
teach.note: Examples: Fatihah 1:7 أَنْعَمْتَ is certain. Say each slowly, clear 'n', then pause for the throat letter. مِنْ هَادٍ and عَلِيمٌ حَكِيمٌ are phrases found in the Qur'an and give good practice with a clear noon.

teach.heading: How to say it
bullets: Move smoothly to the throat letter
teach.note: Model a short clear noon, then the throat letter. Common mistake: humming through the nose. Hold a hand to the nose: it should not buzz.

practice: Circle the throat letter after the noon in أَنْعَمْتَ.
Say this clearly: مِنْ هَادٍ.
independent: Chant the six throat letters five times
Match 6 cards: noon/tanween + throat letter, say 'izhar'
Find izhar in the first page of Al-Fatihah to Al-Baqarah
exit: Name three throat letters.
Do we hum for izhar? Why not?
lessons.homework: Chant the six throat letters to a family member every day and read أَنْعَمْتَ.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: use hand gestures at the throat and a letter card set. Stretch: explain why the noon in مِنْ هَادٍ is izhar.

lessons.title: Iqlab: changing noon into meem
objectives: Know iqlab means changing
Know that the letter baa causes iqlab
Read iqlab with a light humming meem

keywords.def: turning noon sakinah or tanween into a meem
the humming sound from the nose

starter: Is the noon clear (izhar) before ع ? Why?
Say the letter baa with your lips.

teach.heading: Iqlab is a swap
bullets: Iqlab means to change or swap
Noon sakinah or tanween becomes a meem
This happens only before baa ب
teach.note: Use a swap story: the noon passes the baa and puts on a meem hat. Write مِن بَعْدِ with a small meem over the noon. Say it. Ask: what happens to the noon?

teach.heading: Examples
bullets: A small meem is written above
teach.note: Both examples occur many times in the Qur'an. Point out the small meem sign over the noon or tanween in the mushaf. Read slowly: mim-ba'di, sa-mee-'um ba-seer.

teach.heading: How to say it
bullets: Close the lips lightly on the meem
Keep the lips together, then open for baa
teach.note: Practise two counts by tapping the table. Lips must stay closed. Misconception: pressing the lips hard - they should touch gently.

teach.heading: Spot the rule
bullets: Is there a baa after the noon? Iqlab
If not baa, it is a different rule
teach.note: Run a quick spotter game: show words; children shout 'iqlab' or 'no'. Include a few words without baa. Praise careful listening.

practice: Read مِن بَعْدِ and say what happens to the noon.
Which one letter causes iqlab?
independent: Read 6 phrases with iqlab, drawing the small meem
Sort word cards: iqlab or izhar
Hum for two counts with a partner and check the lips
exit: What does iqlab mean?
Read سَمِيعٌ بَصِيرٌ with correct iqlab.
lessons.homework: Read مِن بَعْدِ and سَمِيعٌ بَصِيرٌ aloud each day, with the humming meem for two counts.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: lip-closing mirror practice. Stretch: find a word with iqlab in a surah you know.

lessons.title: Ikhfa: hiding the noon
objectives: Know ikhfa means hiding
Learn the 15 ikhfa letters through a phrase
Read ikhfa examples with ghunnah

keywords.def: hiding the noon sound with ghunnah
a humming sound lasting two counts

starter: Read: مِن شَرِّ. What do you notice?

teach.heading: Ikhfa means hidden
bullets: We hide the noon between izhar and iqlab
The tongue does not touch the gum
teach.note: Demonstrate: say izhar (clear), then ikhfa (hidden) so children hear the difference. The tongue is close to the next letter but the noon is not fully spoken. Ask: where is the tongue?

teach.heading: The 15 letters
bullets: ت ث ج د ذ ز س ش
ص ض ط ظ ف ق ك
15 letters after noon or tanween: ikhfa
teach.note: The 15 ikhfa letters are: ta, tha, jeem, daal, dhaal, zay, seen, sheen, Saad, Daad, Taa, DHaa, faa, qaaf, kaaf. Chant in order to a rhythm. Display the list for reference.

teach.heading: Examples
teach.note: Check: Falaq 113:2 مِن شَرِّ مَا خَلَقَ; Asr 103:2 الْإِنسَانَ لَفِي خُسْرٍ; 82:11 كِرَامًا كَاتِبِينَ. Model: noon hidden, humming two counts, then the next letter.

teach.heading: Light or heavy?
bullets: The mouth shape follows the next letter
Before a heavy letter, ghunnah sounds fuller
Before a light letter, it sounds lighter
teach.note: Contrast مِن شَرِّ (light) with مِن قَبْلِكَ (heavy qaaf, 2:4) as a listening idea only. Key point: same two-count hum, but the mouth shape follows the next letter.

practice: Chant the 15 ikhfa letters.
Is the noon in مِن شَرِّ clear or hidden?
independent: Mark noon/tanween + letter on 8 phrases: izhar, iqlab or ikhfa
Chant 15 ikhfa letters, then find five in Al-Falaq and Al-Asr
Recite Al-Falaq ayah 2 using ikhfa
exit: What does ikhfa mean?
Name three letters that cause ikhfa.
lessons.homework: Chant the 15 ikhfa letters each day and read مِن شَرِّ مَا خَلَقَ.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: colour-code the 15 letters on a poster. Stretch: explain how ikhfa differs from izhar and iqlab.

lessons.unit: Unit 2: Echo, humming and the meem
lessons.title: Qalqalah: the echo letters
objectives: Name the five qalqalah letters
Say a small echo on a quiet letter
Find qalqalah in words

keywords.def: a small echo or bounce when these letters have sukoon
a phrase to remember: ق ط ب ج د

teach.heading: Echo letters
bullets: They echo when they have sukoon
teach.note: Teach the phrase 'qutb jad' and the five letters. Tap the beat. Ask: when do we echo? Only when the letter is quiet (sukoon) or we stop on it.

teach.heading: Examples
teach.note: Use examples from Al-Fil 105:2 يَجْعَلْ, Al-Ikhlas أَحَدٌ (stopping), Al-Masad تَبَّتْ. Do not make the echo into a vowel: it is a bounce, not a fathah.

teach.heading: Three strengths
bullets: End of word when stopping: stronger
teach.note: Keep this as listening, not memorising names. Model three bounces. Misconception: echo as a full extra syllable (e.g. 'ahadu'). Ask children to copy your short bounce.

teach.heading: Practice
teach.note: Use a bouncing hand motion. Pair work: one child recites, the partner raises a hand at each echo.

practice: Say the five echo letters.
Find the qalqalah letter in أَحَدٌ.
independent: Underline echo letters with sukoon in Al-Ikhlas and Al-Falaq
Bounce the echo on 6 words from cards
Recite Al-Ikhlas with echoes at the end of ayat
exit: What are the five qalqalah letters?
What is wrong with adding a vowel to an echo?
lessons.homework: Recite Al-Ikhlas daily with the correct echo on أَحَدٌ.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: gesture bounce and rhythm cards. Stretch: find a strong echo with shaddah in Al-Masad.

lessons.unit: Unit 2: Echo, humming and the meem
lessons.title: Ghunnah: noon and meem with shaddah
objectives: Know ghunnah is the humming sound
Hum for two counts on noon and meem with shaddah
Find these in short surahs

keywords.def: a humming sound from the nose
a mark meaning the letter is doubled

teach.heading: Ghunnah
bullets: A humming sound from the nose
It is part of noon and meem
teach.note: Hum on a gentle 'nnn' and ask children to hold their noses lightly: they should feel a buzz. Two counts means two beats. Ask: where does the sound come from?

teach.heading: Noon and meem with shaddah
bullets: These two letters always hum fully
Hold the ghunnah for two counts
teach.note: Examples: إِنَّا and ثُمَّ. In Al-Kawthar: إِنَّا أَعْطَيْنَاكَ. Model: stress the double letter, humming two counts. Misconception: skipping the hum when reading fast.

teach.heading: In the Qur'an
teach.note: Check: Kawthar 108:1 إِنَّا أَعْطَيْنَاكَ; An-Nas النَّاسِ; Asr إِنَّ الْإِنسَانَ. Have children find each on the page and hum properly.

teach.heading: Hum check
teach.note: Pair task: one hums, one counts on fingers. Reinforce: the hum is short, two counts, not long.

practice: Hum for two counts and clap them.
Which letters hum when they have shaddah?
independent: Find noon or meem with shaddah in An-Nas and Al-Asr and read them
Read 6 words with correct hum (إِنَّا، ثُمَّ، النَّاسِ...)
Recite An-Nas ayat 1-3 with ghunnah
exit: What is ghunnah?
How long do we hum?
lessons.homework: Read An-Nas ayat 1-3 daily and hum two counts on every النَّاسِ.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: finger-count the two beats. Stretch: explain why ghunnah is part of the letter.

lessons.unit: Unit 2: Echo, humming and the meem
lessons.title: Meem sakinah: three rules
objectives: Know the three rules of meem sakinah
Say izhar, ikhfa and idgham for meem
Read examples
starter: Which two letters hum with shaddah?

teach.heading: Meem sakinah
bullets: Three rules depend on the next letter
teach.note: Show أَلَمْ تَرَ and point to the meem sakinah. Ask: what do we check? The next letter. Remind children: the lips close for meem.

teach.heading: Rule one: izhar
bullets: Meem + any letter except baa or meem
teach.note: Al-Fil 105:1-2. Lips close gently on the meem then open. Fuller care before waaw and faa: do not hide the meem. Ask: which letters follow?

teach.heading: Rule two: ikhfa
teach.note: Al-Fil 105:4. Lips touch lightly, hum two counts, then the baa. Do not squeeze. Misconception: confusing with iqlab (noon to meem) - this one is already a meem.

teach.heading: Rule three: idgham
teach.note: Cite 2:249 كَم مِّن فِئَةٍ as the example. The two meems join into one with shaddah-like hum. Practise slowly then at normal pace.

practice: Which rule is used in أَلَمْ تَرَ?
Which letter after meem sakinah gives ikhfa?
independent: Sort 8 phrases into the three meem rules
Recite Al-Fil ayat 1-4, labelling each meem sakinah
Practise the lips and hum with a partner
exit: Name the three rules of meem sakinah.
Which letters cause ikhfa and idgham?
lessons.homework: Read Al-Fil ayat 1-4 daily and find each meem sakinah.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: colour three rules on printed Al-Fil. Stretch: explain why the meem rule involves the lips.

lessons.title: Longer madd: when a hamza follows
objectives: Revise natural madd (2 counts) and its three letters
Know madd is longer when a hamza follows
Hear the difference between 2 and 4 counts
Read madd muttasil and munfasil

keywords.def: connected madd: hamza in the same word
separated madd: hamza in the next word

starter: Which are the three madd letters?
Say a word with madd from Al-Fatihah.

teach.heading: Madd + hamza
bullets: A hamza after a madd letter makes it longer
The length stays the same through the page
teach.note: Explain that the hamza follows the madd letter. Both 4 and 5 counts are accepted in Hafs; choose one for the class and stay consistent.

teach.heading: Muttasil
bullets: Madd letter + hamza in the SAME word
teach.note: An-Nasr starts with إِذَا جَاءَ. Show the madd letter and the hamza joined in one word. Count out loud.

teach.heading: Munfasil
bullets: Madd letter at the end of one word
Hamza at the start of the next word
teach.note: Examples: يَا أَيُّهَا (Al-Kafirun 109:1) and إِنَّا أَعْطَيْنَاكَ (Al-Kawthar 108:1). The madd letter ends one word and the hamza begins the next. Count four, matching muttasil.

teach.heading: Spot the sign
bullets: A wavy sign ~ shows a longer madd
teach.note: Show the madd sign in the mushaf. Pairs: one reads, one taps counts. Misconception: stretching every long vowel. Only when the hamza follows.

practice: Which word has madd muttasil: جَاءَ or قَالَ?
How many counts for the longer madd?
independent: Sort 8 words into natural, muttasil or munfasil
Mark the madd signs in An-Nasr ayah 1
Pair reading with counting on fingers
exit: What causes the longer madd?
Give one word with muttasil.
lessons.homework: Read إِذَا جَاءَ نَصْرُ اللَّهِ daily with a four-count madd.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: colour-coded counts. Stretch: explain the difference between muttasil and munfasil.

lessons.title: Madd at a stop and madd leen
objectives: Know madd 'arid lis-sukoon
Know madd leen
Stretch correctly at the end of ayat

keywords.def: madd when we stop and the last letter is quiet
soft madd on waaw or yaa with sukoon after a fathah

starter: What is the longest madd you know?
How many counts is natural madd?

teach.heading: Madd when we stop
bullets: When we stop, the last letter becomes quiet
The madd before it can be 2, 4 or 6
teach.note: Explain that stopping creates a temporary sukoon. In class, choose 4 counts for simplicity and be consistent. Model الرَّحِيمِ with a stop.

teach.heading: Madd leen
bullets: Waaw or yaa with sukoon after fathah
teach.note: Quraysh 106:1 قُرَيْشٍ and 106:4 خَوْفٍ. This madd happens only when stopping. Explain 'soft' means gentle, not loud.

teach.heading: Practice
bullets: Stop at the end of each ayah
Do not stretch when you join on
teach.note: Distinction: we only stretch these when stopping. Drill: join words (no stretch), then stop (stretch). Let children feel the difference.

teach.heading: Mushaf signs
bullets: Each ayah end is a stop
Take a breath before you begin again
teach.note: Remind children that stopping at the end of ayah is good practice. Model the breath. Common mistake: running out of breath mid-ayah.

practice: Why does the madd get longer when we stop?
Find the madd leen in خَوْفٍ.
independent: Recite Al-Fatihah stopping at each ayah with madd 'arid
Mark madd leen in Quraysh
Compare joining and stopping with a partner
exit: Give one word with madd 'arid.
Do we stretch if we join the ayah to the next? Why?
lessons.homework: Recite Al-Fatihah stopping after each ayah and stretch the final madd correctly.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: visual count bar. Stretch: explain why this madd is called 'temporary'.

lessons.title: Stopping signs (waqf)
objectives: Recognise common stopping signs
Stop or continue correctly
Breathe at the right places
starter: Where do we stop in a surah?
What happens to the last letter when we stop?

teach.heading: Stopping signs
bullets: ج  - you may stop or continue
teach.note: Show these signs from the mushaf and explain their meaning. Remind the class that the signs help us understand the meaning. Stopping in the wrong place can change the meaning of what we read.

teach.heading: Stopping practice
bullets: Take a breath at a stop
teach.note: Use a printed page of Surat Al-Fil or Al-Asr marked with signs. Teacher reads, children raise hands at each stop.

teach.heading: How to stop
bullets: Stop on the last letter with sukoon
Tanween -an: stop with a long 'aa' sound
teach.note: Examples: أَحَدٌ becomes 'ahad'; عَلِيمًا becomes 'aleemaa'; Teach carefully. Keep it simple at this age.

teach.heading: Start again
bullets: Begin at the start of an ayah
Do not begin in the middle of a phrase
Go back to a clear starting point
teach.note: Explain ibtida'. If you run out of breath, go back to the beginning of the phrase. Model both good and poor places to stop.

practice: What does the sign م mean?
How do we stop on a word with tanween -an?
independent: Mark stops on a printed Al-Asr
Recite Al-Asr stopping at each ayah
Pairs: one recites, the other shows green (stop) or red (do not stop) cards
exit: What does لا mean?
Why do we take a breath at a stop?
lessons.homework: Recite Al-Asr to a family member stopping correctly at each ayah.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: colour cards green/red for signs. Stretch: say why wrong stopping can change meaning.

lessons.title: Surat Al-Asr: reading and rules
objectives: Read Al-Asr accurately
Find noon sakinah, ghunnah and madd
Understand the main meaning
starter: Which rule hides the noon before seen?
How many counts for natural madd?

teach.heading: The surah
teach.note: Surah 103 is very short but its message is large: time, loss and success. Recite it once yourself, then echo line by line. Ask: what do we spend every day that is running out? (time)

teach.heading: Ayah 3
teach.note: Meaning in simple words: people are at a loss except those who believe, do good, advise one another to the truth and to patience. Chunk and echo. Ask: what four things save us?

teach.heading: Tajweed spotting
teach.note: Children find each rule on the page. In ayah 3 find natural madds in الَّذِينَ، آمَنُوا، الصَّالِحَاتِ. Praise correct labels.

teach.heading: Learning it
teach.note: Use the routine from Year 1: listen, read, cover. Memorise ayah 1 and 2 today and ayah 3 in the next lesson.

practice: Recite Al-Asr ayah 1 and 2.
Name the rule in الْإِنسَانَ.
independent: Read Al-Asr to a partner, marking tajweed
Memorise ayat 1-2 with listen/read/cover
Draw four actions that save us from loss
exit: Name two things that save us in Al-Asr.
Which rule is in الْإِنسَانَ?
lessons.homework: Recite Al-Asr ayat 1-3 to a family member daily.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: echo-chunk recitation with picture cues for the four actions. Stretch: write one thing you can do to advise a friend to patience.

lessons.title: Surat Al-Kawthar: recite and memorise
objectives: Recite Al-Kawthar accurately
Apply ghunnah and madd
Understand it is a surah of generosity

keywords.def: listening for every rule in a surah

starter: How do we say noon with shaddah?

teach.heading: The surah
teach.note: Meaning: Allah gave the Prophet ﷺ al-Kawthar (abundant good), so pray to your Lord and sacrifice. Chunk and echo. Ask: how should we thank Allah?

teach.heading: Ayah 3
bullets: The one who hates you is cut off
teach.note: Keep the explanation simple: the person who opposes the Prophet ﷺ is the one truly cut off. Ghunnah on إِنَّ. Ask pupils to find the humming letters.

teach.heading: Tajweed spot
teach.note: Children find ghunnah in إِنَّا and إِنَّ, madd in أَعْطَيْنَاكَ, and the middle-of-word echo on the baa of الْأَبْتَرُ (it has a sukoon). Keep the echo light.

teach.heading: Memorise it
bullets: Learn one ayah at a time
teach.note: Use chaining: ayah 1; ayah 1+2; all three. Whole class recites; then volunteers. Praise accuracy over speed.

practice: Recite Al-Kawthar ayah 1.
Find a letter with ghunnah in ayah 1.
independent: Read Al-Kawthar with a partner, marking ghunnah
Memorise ayah 1 and 2, then all three
Recite individually to the teacher
exit: How many ayat are in Al-Kawthar?
Name one rule in إِنَّا.
lessons.homework: Recite Al-Kawthar every day this week until you know it without the mushaf.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: echo and clap the rhythm. Stretch: explain what 'thank Allah' looks like in daily life.

lessons.title: Surat Al-Humazah 104:1-3: hear, understand and memorise
lessons.bigQuestion: Is it ever funny to make fun of someone? How does it feel to be laughed at?
objectives: To memorise Al-Humazah 104:1-3 accurately and recite it with its tajweed
successCriteria: All: say 104:1 to 3 after the teacher
Most: say 104:1 to 3 alone
Some: say what 104:1 warns against

keywords.def: the one who mocks and backbites

hook.text: Is it ever funny to make fun of someone? How does it feel to be laughed at?
hook.a: It hurts. Allah warns those who mock and backbite (104:1); a Muslim's tongue is kind.

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'Woe to every scorner and mocker, who collects wealth and counts it' (Al-Humazah 104:1 to 2). This surah teaches us to keep our tongues kind and not to love money too much.

starter.q: Which way do we read Arabic?

teach.heading: New ayat: Al-Humazah 104:1-3
bullets: Listen first: the teacher recites twice
Follow each word with your finger
teach.note: Begin with isti'adhah and Bismillah. Recite 104:1-3 slowly twice from the mushaf (spoken recitation only, no melody exercises), pointing to each word on the shared screen. The Arabic is the Qur'an in Uthmani script (Hafs 'an 'Asim, Madinah mushaf); check it against the school mushaf.

quote.text: وَيْلٌۭ لِّكُلِّ هُمَزَةٍۢ لُّمَزَةٍ (١) ٱلَّذِى جَمَعَ مَالًۭا وَعَدَّدَهُۥ (٢) يَحْسَبُ أَنَّ مَالَهُۥٓ أَخْلَدَهُۥ (٣)

teach.heading: What the ayat mean
bullets: English helps us understand; only the Arabic is the Qur'an
Big idea: never mock others; money does not last
teach.note: Read the English slowly. Remind pupils: only the Arabic is the Qur'an; any English is a translation of its meaning (here Saheeh International).

head: Ayah
Translation of the meaning (Saheeh International)
rows: Woe to every scorner and mocker
Who collects wealth and [continuously] counts it.

lessons.title: Surat Al-'Asr 103:1-3: hear, understand and memorise
lessons.bigQuestion: Allah swears by time. What are four things that stop us from losing our time?
objectives: To memorise Al-'Asr 103:1-3 accurately and recite it with its tajweed
successCriteria: All: say Al-'Asr after the teacher
Most: say Al-'Asr alone
Some: name the four things in 103:3
lessons.smsc: Moral: using time well; helping friends to be good and patient

hook.text: Allah swears by time. What are four things that stop us from losing our time?
hook.a: Believing, doing good deeds, advising each other to the truth and to patience (103:3).

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'By time, indeed, mankind is in loss, except for those who have believed and done righteous deeds and advised each other to truth and advised each other to patience' (Al-'Asr 103:1 to 3).

starter.q: Recite Al-Humazah 104:6 in your head. How does the next ayah begin?

teach.heading: New ayat: Al-'Asr 103:1-3
bullets: Listen first: the teacher recites twice
Follow each word with your finger
teach.note: Begin with isti'adhah and Bismillah. Recite 103:1-3 slowly twice from the mushaf (spoken recitation only, no melody exercises), pointing to each word on the shared screen. The Arabic is the Qur'an in Uthmani script (Hafs 'an 'Asim, Madinah mushaf); check it against the school mushaf.

quote.text: وَٱلْعَصْرِ (١) إِنَّ ٱلْإِنسَٰنَ لَفِى خُسْرٍ (٢) إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَعَمِلُوا۟ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ وَتَوَاصَوْا۟ بِٱلْحَقِّ وَتَوَاصَوْا۟ بِٱلصَّبْرِ (٣)

teach.heading: What the ayat mean
bullets: English helps us understand; only the Arabic is the Qur'an
Big idea: use your time for good
teach.note: Read the English slowly. Remind pupils: only the Arabic is the Qur'an; any English is a translation of its meaning (here Saheeh International).

head: Ayah
Translation of the meaning (Saheeh International)
rows: Except for those who have believed and done righteous deeds and advised each other to truth and advised each other to patience.

teach.heading: Listen and repeat: mics in turn
teach.note: Talaqqi (تلقي): learning recitation by hearing it from the teacher. Work through 103:1-3 one ayah at a time. Keep a visible order of names (the register) so every pupil gets a turn across the week. Unmute only the pupils whose turn it is; everyone else whispers along with mics muted.

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: Launch the Teams poll. Read the results, then explain the right answer.

check.q: How many things save us from loss in 103:3?
check.why: Belief, good deeds, advising to truth, advising to patience.

practice.q: Chunk and link Al-'Asr 103:1-3 with the teacher.
practice.model: I do: chunk 103:1-3. Ayah 1: 3 times looking, 3 times without looking. Then ayah 2 the same way. Then link: recite 1 and 2 together twice. Finish by reciting the whole chunk once without the mushaf.

independent.q: Listening turns: today's group says 103:1-3 to the teacher, one by one. Everyone else: say it softly 3 times looking, 3 times without.
independent.a: Pupil recites with no help; the teacher marks hifdh and tajweed on the rubric and gives one target.
independent.model: The teacher shows the 3-3-link method once: read the ayah 3 times looking, say it 3 times without looking, then link it to the ayah before it. Rota: names on screen, about 90 seconds each, so every pupil is heard at least once a week; the teacher marks the rubric and gives one target.

independent.q: Tell a friend one good thing you did with your time today.

exit.q: Al-'Asr 103:2: «إِنَّ ...» Which word comes next?
exit.a: ٱلْإِنسَٰنَ

exit.q: Back to our ponder: Allah swears by time. What are four things that stop us from losing our time?
exit.a: Believing, doing good deeds, advising each other to the truth and to patience (103:3).
